<p id="mwEA"><b id="mwEQ">Boids</b> is an <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Artificial_life" title="Artificial life" id="mwEg">artificial life</a> algorithm, developed by <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Craig_Reynolds_(computer_graphics)" title="Craig Reynolds (computer graphics)" id="mwEw">Craig Reynolds</a> in 1986, which simulates the <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Flocking_(behavior)" title="Flocking (behavior)" class="mw-redirect" id="mwFA">flocking</a> behaviour of <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bird" title="Bird" id="mwFQ">birds</a>, and related group motion. His paper on this topic was published in 1987 in the proceedings of the <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Association_for_Computing_Machinery" title="Association for Computing Machinery" id="mwFg">ACM</a> <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/SIGGRAPH" title="SIGGRAPH" id="mwFw">SIGGRAPH</a> conference.<sup about="#mwt9" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-1" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{"name":"ref","attrs":{},"body":{"id":"mw-reference-text-cite_note-1"}}"><a href="#cite_note-1" id="mwGA"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwGQ"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwGg">[</span>1<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwGw">]</span></span></a></sup> The name "boid" corresponds to a shortened version of "bird-oid object", which refers to a bird-like object, as well as referencing the stereotypical <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_York_accent" title="New York accent" id="mwHA">New York pronunciation</a> of 'bird' as <span class="rt-commentedText nowrap" about="#mwt5" typeof="mw:Transclusion" id="mwHQ" data-mw="{"name":"ref","attrs":{},"body":{"id":"mw-reference-text-cite_note-3"}}"><a href="#cite_note-3" id="mwIg"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwIw"><span class="cite-bracket" Reynolds' boid model is one example of a larger general concept, for which many other variations have been developed since. The closely related work of Ichiro Aoki is noteworthy because it was published in 1982 – five years <i id="mwJg">before</i> Reynolds' boids paper.<sup about="#mwt19" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-4" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{"name":"ref","attrs":{},"body":{"id":"mw-reference-text-cite_note-4"}}"><a href="#cite_note-4" id="mwJw"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwKA"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwKQ">[</span>4<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwKg">]</span></span></a></sup></p>

<meta property="mw:PageProp/toc" id="mwLQ" data-mw="{"autoGenerated":true}"></section><section data-mw-section-id="1" id="mwLg" aria-labelledby="Model_details"><div class="mw-heading mw-heading2"><h2 id="Model_details">Model details</h2><span class="mw-editsection"><span class="mw-editsection-bracket">[</span><a href="/w/index.php?title=Boids&action=edit&section=1" title="Edit section: Model details"><span>edit</span></a><span class="mw-editsection-bracket">]</span></span></div>
<p id="mwLw">Like most artificial life simulations, Boids is an example of <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Emergence" title="Emergence" id="mwMA">emergent</a> behavior; that is, the complexity of Boids arises from the interaction of individual agents (the boids, in this case) adhering to a set of simple rules. The rules applied in the simplest Boids world are as follows:</p>
<ul id="mwMQ"><li id="mwMg"><b id="mwMw">separation</b>: <a rel="mw:WikiLink/Interwiki" href="https://en.wiktionary.org/wiki/steer#Verb" title="wikt:steer" class="extiw" id="mwNA">steer</a> to avoid crowding local flockmates</li>
<li id="mwNQ"><b id="mwNg">alignment</b>: steer towards the average heading of local flockmates</li>
<li id="mwNw"><b id="mwOA">cohesion</b>: steer to move towards the average position (center of mass) of local flockmates</li></ul>

<p id="mwOQ">More complex rules can be added, such as obstacle avoidance and goal seeking.</p>

<p id="mwOg">The basic model has been extended in several different ways since Reynolds proposed it. For instance, Delgado-Mata et<span typeof="mw:Entity" id="mwOw"> </span>al.<sup about="#mwt24" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-5" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{"name":"ref","attrs":{},"body":{"id":"mw-reference-text-cite_note-5"}}"><a href="#cite_note-5" id="mwPA"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwPQ"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwPg">[</span>5<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwPw">]</span></span></a></sup> extended the basic model to incorporate the effects of fear. Olfaction was used to transmit emotion between animals, through pheromones modelled as particles in a free expansion gas. Hartman and Benes<sup about="#mwt27" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-6" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{"name":"ref","attrs":{},"body":{"id":"mw-reference-text-cite_note-6"}}"><a href="#cite_note-6" id="mwQA"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwQQ"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwQg">[</span>6<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwQw">]</span></span></a></sup> introduced a complementary force to the alignment that they call the change of leadership. This steer defines the chance of the boid to become a leader and try to escape.</p>

<p id="mwRA">The movement of Boids can be characterized as either chaotic (splitting groups and wild behaviour) or orderly. Unexpected behaviours, such as splitting flocks and reuniting after avoiding obstacles, can be considered emergent.</p>

<p id="mwRQ">The boids framework is often used in computer graphics, providing realistic-looking representations of flocks of birds and other creatures, such as schools of fish or herds of animals. It was for instance used in the 1998 video game <i id="mwRg"><a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Half-Life_(video_game)" title="Half-Life (video game)" id="mwRw">Half-Life</a></i> for the flying bird-like creatures seen at the end of the game on <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Locations_of_Half-Life#Xen" title="Locations of Half-Life" class="mw-redirect" id="mwSA">Xen</a>, named "boid" in the game files.</p>

<p id="mwSQ">The Boids model can be used for direct control and stabilization of teams of simple unmanned ground vehicles (UGV)<sup about="#mwt30" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-7" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{"name":"ref","attrs":{},"body":{"id":"mw-reference-text-cite_note-7"}}"><a href="#cite_note-7" id="mwSg"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwSw"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwTA">[</span>7<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwTQ">]</span></span></a></sup> or <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Micro_air_vehicle" title="Micro air vehicle" id="mwTg">micro aerial vehicles</a> (MAV)<sup about="#mwt33" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-8" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{"name":"ref","attrs":{},"body":{"id":"mw-reference-text-cite_note-8"}}"><a href="#cite_note-8" id="mwTw"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwUA"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwUQ">[</span>8<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwUg">]</span></span></a></sup> in <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Swarm_robotics" title="Swarm robotics" id="mwUw">swarm robotics</a>. For stabilization of heterogeneous UAV-UGV teams, the model was adapted for using onboard relative localization by Saska et<span typeof="mw:Entity" id="mwVA"> </span>al.<sup about="#mwt36" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-9" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{"name":"ref","attrs":{},"body":{"id":"mw-reference-text-cite_note-9"}}"><a href="#cite_note-9" id="mwVQ"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwVg"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwVw">[</span>9<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwWA">]</span></span></a></sup></p>

<p id="mwWQ">At the time of proposal, Reynolds' approach represented a giant step forward compared to the traditional techniques used in computer animation for motion pictures. The first animation created with the model was <i id="mwWg"><a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stanley_and_Stella_in:_Breaking_the_Ice" title="Stanley and Stella in: Breaking the Ice" id="mwWw">Stanley and Stella in: Breaking the Ice</a></i> (1987), followed by a feature film debut in <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tim_Burton" title="Tim Burton" id="mwXA">Tim Burton</a>'s film <i id="mwXQ"><a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Batman_Returns" title="Batman Returns" id="mwXg">Batman Returns</a></i> (1992) with computer-generated bat swarms and armies of penguins marching through the streets of Gotham City.<sup about="#mwt39" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-10" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{"name":"ref","attrs":{},"body":{"id":"mw-reference-text-cite_note-10"}}"><a href="#cite_note-10" id="mwXw"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwYA"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwYQ">[</span>10<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwYg">]</span></span></a></sup></p>

<p id="mwYw">The boids model has been used for other interesting applications. It has been applied to automatically program Internet multi-channel radio stations.<sup about="#mwt42" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-11" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{"name":"ref","attrs":{},"body":{"id":"mw-reference-text-cite_note-11"}}"><a href="#cite_note-11" id="mwZA"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwZQ"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwZg">[</span>11<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwZw">]</span></span></a></sup> It has also been used for visualizing information<sup about="#mwt46" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-12" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{"name":"ref","attrs":{},"body":{"id":"mw-reference-text-cite_note-12"}}"><a href="#cite_note-12" id="mwaA"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwaQ"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwag">[</span>12<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwaw">]</span></span></a></sup> and for optimization tasks.<sup about="#mwt49" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-13" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{"name":"ref","attrs":{},"body":{"id":"mw-reference-text-cite_note-13"}}"><a href="#cite_note-13" id="mwbA"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwbQ"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwbg">[</span>13<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwbw">]</span></span></a></sup></p>

<p id="mwcA">Biologist <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Richard_Dawkins" title="Richard Dawkins" id="mwcQ">Richard Dawkins</a> references the Boids model in his 2009 book <i id="mwcg"><a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Greatest_Show_on_Earth:_The_Evidence_for_Evolution" title="The Greatest Show on Earth: The Evidence for Evolution" id="mwcw">The Greatest Show on Earth: The Evidence for Evolution</a></i>.<sup about="#mwt52" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-14" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{"name":"ref","attrs":{},"body":{"id":"mw-reference-text-cite_note-14"}}"><a href="#cite_note-14" id="mwdA"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwdQ"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwdg">[</span>14<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwdw">]</span></span></a></sup></p>
